svg.text: C-B SANDWICH — GN trays on a slide, flipped as clamshells
Bought Gastronorm trays ride under a bridge of fixed heads; turning is done by clamping two trays rim to rim and inverting the pair.
shaking hob ±15 mm at 3 Hz, < 100 N
PREP LANE (side view): the tray moves, the heads stay

g.text: GN 1/3 tray · purple: silicone apron liner · red: meat slice
bar holds the liner hem, tray drives back:
the liner rolls the slice up (sushi mat)
mustard stripe laid while the tray passes
bacon, onion, gherkin on the leading edge

svg.text: turns about the long axis: the whole set is flipped at once
coil, glass and tray shake together (carriage)
reverse the stroke to walk back
GN TRAYS (top view, 0.6 px/mm), all bought
same trays: storage box, pan, oven tin,
weak point: no native round work

g.text: 1/7 A meat slice lies on a silicone apron in a GN 1/3 tray; the tray rides under a bridge of fixed heads.
2/7 Tray passes under the paste slot: a mustard stripe is laid by the tray's own travel.
3/7 Piece doser drops bacon, onion and gherkin on the leading edge; the tray runs on to the apron bar.
4/7 Apron bar hooks the liner hem; the tray drives back and the liner rolls the slice up.
5/7 The finished roll lies seam-down; four of them are seared side by side in a thermoplate.
6/7 Clamshell flip: a second tray is clamped upside down on top and the pair is turned over.
7/7 Shaking hob: slow-out / fast-back stroke makes the pieces walk and roll over — stirring with no tool.
